disputed.question: Is a server-version downgrade (8.0 to 7.0) blocked by the control plane, and what error does it return? (DECISIONS topic 11, open item 2)
disputed.reason: The observed part holds. The 8.0 to 7.0 update exited 0 with empty stderr after 93.54 s. The activity log shows the write Started and Accepted at 23:16:14Z and Succeeded at 23:17:47.8Z with statusMessage null. show then returned 7.0, Succeeded and Ready. The closing sentence 'The control plane will not stop an accidental downgrade' goes further than that. It generalises from one downgrade, one version pair and one shape (M30, 1 shard, PremiumSSDv2, HA off). The Q&A case that ended UpdateFailed/409 was a Free-tier cluster, and lower targets (6.0, 5.0), other tiers, HA and multi-shard clusters were not tried. It should say 'did not stop this downgrade'. The kit advice ('do not lower --server-version') still stands.

disputed.question: What does the downgrade change on the data plane?
disputed.reason: 'Only the advertised compatibility level' was not observed. The test read only hello (ok, maxWireVersion, minWireVersion, msg, internal) and buildInfo (version, versionArray, maxBsonObjectSize, ok, key list). It ran no 8.0-only command or operator before and after the switch. Drivers decide features from maxWireVersion, so behaviour that applications see does change. m-txn-bulk saw PyMongo 4.20.1 send client-level bulkWrite at wire 25 and get code 2 BadValue. ENGINE-TESTS saw PyMongo refuse the same call client-side at wire 21. Neither case was re-tested after the downgrade. It should read 'of the fields checked, only the advertised level changed'. The vs_open_source 'same' holds only for maxWireVersion 21 and buildInfo 7.0.0. According to the engine-tests-1.2 raw reports, hello.internal.documentdb_versions (2.2-1/2.3.0/12.1-1 vs 1.2-0/1.2.0) and kind ('azuredocumentdb' vs '') still differ from documentdb-local 1.2.0. m-hosts also found that the managed hello adds endpointName and operationTime. 'Partly same' is more accurate.

disputed.question: Does the CLI help warn that a lower --server-version downgrades?
disputed.reason: The help-text finding is observed: there is no upgrade-only rule and no warning. The extra claim, that 'defaults to latest' is misleading on update because leaving the flag out keeps the current version, rests on two things. One is a source reading that no raw record captures. The other is m-entra's update of auth modes only, which left the cluster at 8.0. That observation cannot tell the two readings apart, because 8.0 was both the current and the latest version. The reviewer read the installed 1.0.0 source (/Users/julietai/.azure/cliextensions/documentdb/azext_documentdb/aaz/latest/documentdb/mongocluster/_update.py): MongoClustersGet, then InstanceUpdateByJson/Generic, then a PATCH of the whole instance at api-version 2026-06-01. The claim is therefore probably right, but it comes from the source and should be labelled that way, not 'observed'. Observing it needs an update without --server-version on a cluster below the latest version, and that would change the cluster.

disputed.question: Which extension version does the dynamic install pick?
disputed.reason: Observed: the stable 1.0.0 was installed (preview false; documentdb-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl, 97,139 bytes). 'A fresh agent machine therefore gets the same 1.0.0 command surface' generalises from one fresh AZURE_CONFIG_DIR on the same azure-cli 2.89.1 install at one moment. The choice depends on that az version's preview-install default and on what the extension index holds at install time; a stable 1.1.0 would be picked once it ships. It should be scoped to 'az 2.89.1, default config, 2026-11-25'. The name '1.1.0b2' also comes from DECISIONS topic 11's index listing, not from this run: the warning names no version and the 104-byte extensionIndex.json was not read.

disputed.question: What happens instead when az has a TTY?
disputed.reason: Observed: the prompt text, the (Y/n) default, the decline message, exit code 2 (b8b's correction of timed_out holds) and that nothing was installed (b9 has no cliextensions/). 'An agent or CI step that runs az on a pseudo-terminal and never answers will hang at this prompt' was not observed: the script answered after 1.47 s and az exited 0.07 s later. It is a sound inference from a prompt that blocks for input, but it should be labelled as an inference. EOF on the pty was not tested.

extra_observations: Secrets: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-julietai-claude/40f65f7c-640c-44c6-8eab-a8434709e1ff/scratchpad/managed-tests/m-cli/raw/.ids.json is a mode-600 masking-key cache that common.py _load_ids() writes from `az account show` and `az ad signed-in-user show`. It held the signed-in user's e-mail address in clear, plus the subscription id, tenant id, home tenant id, object id and the tenant default domain, which contains the e-mail's local part. These are redacted in place to <email-masked>, <subscription-id-masked>, <tenant-id-masked>, <object-id-masked> and <tenant-domain-masked>. The generic 'Default Directory' tenant name and the generic subscription offer name were left. A re-scan of every m-cli file (including __pycache__) finds no e-mail address, no MANAGED_PASS in raw or URL-encoded form, no MANAGED_URI or MANAGED_GLOBAL_URI, no JWT, no URI with credentials, and no GUID other than the scratchpad session id. report.json and raw/steps.jsonl were already clean. The tester's note 8 ('A leak scan of every file in the m-cli folder found none of them') was therefore wrong.

Consequence of the redaction: if an m-cli script is rerun, common.py loads the placeholders. GUIDs and e-mail addresses are still masked by regex, but the tenant default domain is no longer masked by name. Deleting the file would make the next import write the real values again. Keeping these ids in memory only would be safer.

Cluster state, from one read-only show by the reviewer at 2026-11-25T23:37:05Z: ddb-samples-shared is still serverVersion 7.0, Succeeded, Ready, lastModifiedAt 23:16:14.2Z, so nobody has reverted the downgrade. The task context ('reports hello.maxWireVersion 25') and ENGINE-TESTS.md's note that the managed service reports wire version 25 no longer describe this cluster. Findings that depend on wire 25, such as m-txn-bulk (h) on client-level bulkWrite, would not reproduce until someone runs `az documentdb mongocluster update -g documentdb-samples-rg -n ddb-samples-shared --server-version 8.0`. The reviewer did not run it.

Open-source comparison: ENGINE-TESTS.md states wire 21 and MongoDB 7.0.0 for 0.117, but only wire 21 for 1.2.0. The engine-tests-1.2 raw reports confirm buildInfo 7.0.0, documentdb_versions [1.2-0, 1.2.0] and kind '' for 1.2.0. So the 'different' verdict for a0 is correct. The 'same' verdicts for a5 and a6 are correct for maxWireVersion and buildInfo.version only. CLI and control-plane steps are correctly n/a.

The 8.0.0 buildInfo before the downgrade comes from sibling tests, not from this run. The reviewer confirmed that m-hosts, m-query and m-txn-bulk (20:56Z and 21:10Z) recorded 8.0.0. This test recorded only hello before the downgrade (wire 25 at 23:15:57Z).

Extra support for conclusion 5: the b3 inventory shows two command logs, unknown_command (pid 17224) followed by documentdb_mongocluster_list (pid 17227). This is direct evidence that az re-ran the command in a second process after installing the extension.

Corroboration: m-entra's earlier update (auth modes, 155.4 s) also printed provisioningState Updating in its returned body. 'Poll show; do not trust the update output' has now been seen twice. The installed source uses LRO final-state-via 'location', which fits a stale final body. The duration (93.5 s) is a single observation for a downgrade on one shape.

Reproducibility: some records have no producing script in the folder. These are the c1 refused_locally / not_attempted records, the c9 show and resource-list checks (whose query differs from step_c.py's SHOW_QUERY), b6b and b8b; all were written ad hoc. step_b.py was edited after it ran (mtime 23:21:58Z). b6's recorded command is an immediate rmtree, but the remove() on disk now waits 15 s and 20 s and retries; the timed_out fix is noted in a code comment. The scripts on disk would not reproduce b6 or b8 exactly.

p0: the summary handed to the reviewer cites a Bash `[ -t 0 ]` check ('stdin: not a tty'). That check is not in raw/steps.jsonl or report.json; only Python sys.stdin.isatty() == false is recorded. The conclusion still follows. The reviewer's environment has no AZURE_* variables, and the prompt in the TTY run rules out use_dynamic_install=yes_without_prompt being set.

The reading 'every other property unchanged' covers only the queried properties: tier, storage, shardCount, HA, auth modes and public network access. Not measured: data-plane availability during the switch; whether data, indexes or preview features (FullTextSearch) behave the same after the downgrade; whether an upgrade back to 8.0 works.
Both temporary config dirs (azcfg-m-cli.*) were confirmed absent at review time. No other managed-tests folder contains MANAGED_PASS or a real e-mail address (checked by count only).
summary: The test is sound and its core findings follow from the raw records. (a) The 8.0 to 7.0 downgrade was accepted. The CLI exited 0 with empty stderr after 93.54 s. The activity log shows the write Accepted, then Succeeded about 94 s later with statusMessage null. The cluster settled at 7.0, Succeeded and Ready, and hello maxWireVersion fell from 25 to 21 with documentdb_versions unchanged. buildInfo then read 7.0.0; the earlier 8.0.0 comes from sibling tests the reviewer checked. (b) Without a TTY, the first `az documentdb` call in a fresh config dir installed the stable 1.0.0 without prompting and re-ran the command; exit code 1 came only from the missing login. On a pty, az prompted (Y/n), and declining exited 2 with nothing installed. (c) Never ran: local permissions refused the create, and it is correctly marked inconclusive. Five conclusions claim more than was observed. 'The control plane will not stop an accidental downgrade' rests on one case. 'Only the advertised compatibility level changes' was not tested, and the open-source verdict 'same' holds only for maxWireVersion and buildInfo.version. 'Defaults to latest is misleading on update' rests on a source reading plus m-entra evidence that cannot tell the readings apart; the installed source supports it. 'A fresh agent machine gets 1.0.0' generalises from one config dir. 'Will hang on a pty' is an inference. secrets_found is true. raw/.ids.json held the user's e-mail, subscription, tenant and object ids, and a tenant domain derived from the e-mail; all are now redacted in place. Every other file is clean. The shared cluster is still at serverVersion 7.0 as of 23:37:05Z.
